newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares cruise to new high over 1,500 pts.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares cruise to new high over 1,500 pts.

text.p: Banks led Greek shares to new highs in early Monday trade with the general index breaking the 1,500 barrier with an 1.83 percent jump shortly after trading started.
Market participants noted that the rally which started in late 1996 was far from reaching its peak.
"The index will find its way to higher levels by the end of this year," said Filippos Boukouvalas, fund manager of Kosmos-SocGen mutual funds.
"We believe the bull market will perform strongly in the coming months," said Kappa Securities in its weekly report.
Rapidly improving macroeconomic indicators and corporate performance have been crucial to the market's take-off according to market participants.
"The drop in interest rates, which has been accomodated by falling inflation, raised demand for alternatives to investing in treasury paper," said Boukouvalas.
The rise has so far been very concentrated into bank shares which typically attract the first inflow of funds into the equity market, he said.
But the rally will be better based when funds start being chanelled into the broader market.
The Athens general share index was 1.59 percent up at 1,508.65 from Friday's 1,484.97 close after 20 minutes of trading, having reached an intra-day high of 1,512.14 shortly after the market opened.
Banks were up 1.90 percent and construction was trading 1.01 percent higher.
Turnover amounted to 3.5 billion drachmas on 1.0 million shares traded. Advancers led decliners 124 to 27 with 17 stocks unchanged on 168 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,104.0-1,134.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 185 drachmas at 6,500.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted unchanged at $66.65-$68.34. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted unchanged at 2,359-2,559 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted unchanged at $15.15-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
